title: Chain-of-Sketch: Enabling Global Visual Reasoning

model.params_source: assumed (the paper states only that tool calling was disabled and that images were sent at 512x512 in the API's high-resolution mode; no decoding parameters are given). o4-mini ignores temperature; max_tokens is set generously because the prompt asks for reasoning before the verdict.

task.subset_rule: the paper's 1,000 test samples for Cycles with 6 nodes (500 per class)
task.approximation: BLOCKING - the 1,000 images are neither released nor reproducible from a released generator, and the runner cannot attach images.

items.source: procedurally generated 448x448 cycle images, rendered to 512x512 for the API (Appendix C.1 gives the generation algorithm: 2n nodes placed at random angles on an invisible circle of radius 220 with a minimum separation of epsilon radians, joined by 2n edges forming either one 2n-cycle (label 1) or two n-cycles (label 0), equiprobably). No dataset link, code link or generator seed appears anywhere in the paper.
items.config_or_split: Cycles, 6 nodes, zero-shot 'Prompt' setting (the 'ICL' column uses the same images with four in-context example images)
items.fields_note: The label the prompt asks for is 1 or 2; the dataset's own label is 1 = connected (single cycle) and 0 = two cycles, so any re-implementation must map 0 -> 'output: 2'.

prompt.user_template: This image contains {NODES} nodes which are shown by large white filled dots. There are {NODES} edges between the nodes. Does the image contain a single closed cycle or two separate closed cycles? (A cycles is a closed path which passes through a number of nodes so when there is a single cycle all nodes are reachable from each other and when answer is 2 there are two separate connected components in the graph.) Provide your reasoning and end your answer with “output: 1” or “output: 2”. <task img>

placeholders.task_img: NOT EXPRESSIBLE: <task img> is the 512x512 cycle image, attached to the same user message in the API's high-resolution mode

prompt.few_shot: none for this cell (the ICL column of Table 1 prepends four example images, two per class)
prompt.source_location: Table 5 (Appendix C.5), row 'Cycles with no in-context examples'
prompt.verbatim: full, with two repairs of PDF damage: the line-break hyphenation is undone and the placeholder <NODES> is written as the config slot {NODES} (set to 6 for the 6-node row). The typographic quotes around output: 1 / output: 2 are kept as printed.

output.postprocess: take the last output: n in the reply; an unparsable reply counts as wrong
output.parse_paper: the prompt requires the answer to end with output: 1 or output: 2

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of the 1,000 test images whose predicted class (1 = single cycle, 2 = two cycles) matches the gold class
metric.original_location: Table 1, row Cycles 6 nodes, column o4-mini / Prompt (o3 scores 63.4 and GPT-4o 61.9 on the same cell; the caption gives a 95% CI of about +-3%)

cost.est_note: 1,000 images x 3 seeds at o4-mini prices; one 512x512 high-detail image plus a few thousand reasoning tokens per call. Not a dry-run number: --prepare cannot build these items.

open_points: runner gap: image input; the task IS an image and the runner sends text only.

Items unavailable: no dataset or generator is released. Appendix C.1 specifies the algorithm well enough to re-implement (node angles, minimum separation, one 2n-cycle vs two n-cycles, 448x448 canvas), but node radius drawing style, line width, anti-aliasing and the 448 -> 512 rescale are unspecified, and re-implementing the stimulus generator would make this our own benchmark rather than the paper's. A human must decide whether that substitution is acceptable.
Chance is 50% and the paper's own CI is about +-3 points, so a 1,000-item run is the minimum useful size; a cost cap that subsets the items would make the comparison uninformative.
notes: The same table gives the rectangular-maze rows and the four-shot ICL columns with the prompts printed in the same Table 5, so any image-capable successor to this config can cover them without new prompt work. || Appendix C.5 records the checkpoints as gpt-4o-2024-08-06, o4-mini-2025-04-16 and o3-2025-04-16 and notes that 512x512 in high-resolution mode worked best.
runner_gaps: items: no released dataset or generator
